293858017_3ea21a90.text: Distribution of 26RFa mRNA in the hypothalamus (from Bregma -1.06 to -1.70 mm) using RNAscope in situ hybridization technology indicated the presence of a large population of 26RFa-expressing cells in the LHA and a smaller population of positive cells located ventrally (Fig. 1A). Double-labeling experiments showed an important co-expression of 26RFa and orexin mRNAs in the same cells of the LHA (Fig. 1A, B). Indeed, quantitative analysis revealed that 90% of the 26RFa-positive cells express orexin mRNA and, conversely, 86% of the orexinexpressing cells co-express 26RFa mRNA (Fig. 1B). This molecular overlap was confirmed by immunohistochemical analysis of hypothalamic slices from 26RFa-tdTomato mice, showing important co-localization between tdTomato and orexin A antibodies (Fig. 1C, D). Quantitative analysis revealed that 86% of tdTomato cells are labelled by orexin-A antibodies and, conversely, 62% of the orexin-immunostained cells correspond to tdTomato cells (Fig. 1D)

293858017_ed72744c.text: .Finally, NeuN labelling further indicated that 66% of 26RFa/orexin expressing cells present in the LHA correspond to neurons (Fig. 1E). Together, these findings identify a previously uncharacterized lateral hypothalamic neuronal population co-expressing 26RFa and orexin

293858017_fbe3074b.text: Here, using complementary neuroanatomical and molecular approaches, we provide a detailed characterization of this population and show that 26RFa-expressing cells in the LHA display extensive co-expression with orexin (~90%), while approximately two-thirds of these cells exhibit a neuronal identity (~66%). These findings support very recent observations of 26RFaorexin co-expression (Seifinejad et al, 2023) and identify a discrete lateral hypothalamic peptidergic population within the LHA, referred to here as 26RFa/ orexin neurons. The presence of a fraction of non-neuronal 26RFa-expressing cells suggests additional cellular complexity within this hypothalamic population that deserves further investigation

293858017_2a9fab34.text: .In the present study, we show that central administration of orexin A produces closely related metabolic effects, including an anti- hyperglycemic response associated with increased insulin production and decreased insulin sensitivity. Thus, 26RFa/orexin neurons contain two neuropeptides that exert convergent central actions on glucose regulation

293858017_a30a10c5.text: .Strikingly, chemogenetic activation of LHA 26RFa/orexin neurons enhances the hyperglycemic response to a peripheral glucose load while simultaneously stimulating pancreatic insulin secretion. Notably, activation has no detectable effect on basal glycemia, insulin sensitivity, or hepatic glucose production.
